title: We Come Our Sabbath Hymn to Raise
description: We Come Our Sabbath Hymn to Raise in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 759 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Death of a Scholar”, where the book credits them to the S. S. Choir.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: We come our Sab-bath hymn to raise, Our ear-nest, hum-ble prayer to pour; One voice is hushed, its notes of praise Shall min-gle here with ours no more.

lines: We come our Sabbath hymn to raise,
Our earnest, humble prayer to pour;
One voice is hushed, its notes of praise
Shall mingle here with ours no more.
The lips are still, the eye is dim,
That brightly beamed with joy and love;
The spirit, it hath gone to Him
Who freely gave it from above.
We will not weep, for Jesus said,
But pray that our young hearts be led

credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
